title: Polypropylene skid and loop fabrication | Aquemi
meta: PP skids and loops built in our shop: qualified thermoplastic welders, a numbered joint log, material certificates for PP resin and pipe, pressure-tested before FAT.
headline: Trace any joint back to its welder and material
lead: We build polypropylene (PP) skids and loops in our shop, every product-contact joint numbered and logged with its welder, settings and material.

blocks.intro: A joint inside a finished skid is hard to re-inspect: evidence is made at the bench.

items.q: What certificates come with the PP resin and pipe?
items.a: [certificate type for PP resin and pipe, and what it states: resin grade, lot, compliance]. Each lot is logged against its marking on receipt.

items.q: Who is qualified to make a joint?
items.a: Only welders qualified to [welder qualification standard for thermoplastics, for example DVS 2212], on the method they use. Qualifications are in the dossier.

items.q: What happens to a rejected joint?
items.a: It is cut out and remade. The replacement gets a new number and its own inspection, linked to the rejected joint. Rejection rate reported: [joint rejection rate reported, yes or no].

items.q: Can we audit the shop and see a real joint log?
items.a: Yes. Shop: [shop location, city and province]. Sample log: [redacted joint log shareable under NDA, yes or no].

items.q: How is a PP loop cleaned before first use?
items.a: [pre-commissioning flush and cleaning procedure for PP]. The final rinse is PW, run to conductivity and TOC limits and recorded.
